title: Calidad, limpieza y contratos de datos
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S15 is AUDITED_REPAIR_REQUIRED. Schema-driven ingestion, row/column reconciliation, clean provenance and Parquet are not safe prerequisites. S10 process exit status remains MISCONCEPTION_RISK.

roadmap_expectation.T1: nulls and field policies; indicators and imputation limits
roadmap_expectation.T2: exact duplicates and conflicts; keys, cardinality and evidence preservation
roadmap_expectation.T3: string/number/date/category normalization; plausible outliers vs errors
roadmap_expectation.T4: schema and cross-field rules; metrics, quarantine and audit trail
roadmap_expectation.gate: quality suite that fails explainably on schema drift, quantifies loss and never silently repairs data

live_site.note: No current hydrated S16 render could be verified in the available environment; no source/deployment parity claim is made.

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: Treat the eight isolated mini-demos as if they already form one fail-closed gate, even though no single input flows through them into disjoint clean/quarantine outputs and derived metrics.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: S16 uses S17's groupby/transform and S18's median/quantile/IQR/z-score before those concepts are taught; it also assumes process exit semantics that remain unsafe from S10.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: An optional field whose null rate is below the cap is safe to impute; the lesson does not adequately separate permission to be null from semantic permission to invent a replacement value.

confirmed_findings.location: tagline + opening p5 + reference p3 + T4-B
confirmed_findings.evidence: The section promises a fail-closed quality suite, but each theory block operates on a fresh hand-built DataFrame. T4-B manually creates clean/quarantine tables instead of deriving them from the null, duplicate, normalization, schema and cross-field rules taught earlier.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S15 ingestion basics only; S16 itself must teach the quality-gate composition.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson teaches isolated checks but never shows the causal pipeline raw input → rule results → disjoint clean/quarantine → metrics → pass/fail.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can reproduce eight demos yet still be unable to build the integrated quality gate promised by the tagline and roadmap.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Composition is the section-level performance; without it, the gate is vocabulary plus fragments rather than a worked mechanism.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one compact theory example `run_quality_gate(raw, contract)` that reuses the taught checks and derives clean, quarantine, metrics and audit events from one input.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text states `NaN` means «no sé». In pandas/NumPy-backed columns NaN can be used as a missing-value sentinel, but IEEE NaN means Not a Number and does not encode why a value is absent or invalid.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S14 left NaN semantics unsafe; S16 must not collapse numeric NaN and business meaning.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A storage sentinel is equated with one semantic cause.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can treat every NaN as evidence that the source value was simply unknown, even when it arose from coercion or numeric computation.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Quality rules depend on distinguishing source missingness, conversion failure and invalid numeric results.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say: «En estas columnas pandas usa NaN como marca de valor faltante; NaN no explica por qué falta. Conserva además el motivo: ausente en origen, coerción fallida, etc.»

confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening distinguishes absent, not-applicable and real zero, but the executable policy reduces fields to required|optional. T1-B then allows median imputation for an optional field solely when its null rate is below a cap.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic missing-value identification; semantic missingness policy is new here.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Optionality answers whether null is allowed, not whether replacing it with a value is semantically valid.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can infer `optional + null_rate <= cap => safe to impute` and invent values where null actually means not applicable or deliberately unknown.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The section's central ethical/data-quality claim is never inventing silent data; this shortcut can do exactly that.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Extend the field policy with an explicit null action/meaning such as required_fail, optional_keep_null or optional_impute(method=...), and state that the cap limits volume but does not authorize imputation.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The conflict detector uses `groupby(...).transform('nunique')`, but the authoritative roadmap schedules groupby/agg/transform for S17. S16 gives syntax but no mental model of grouping, per-group aggregation or transform shape preservation.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Dictionaries/sets and pandas selection; groupby/transform is not yet creditable.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A next-section abstraction is used as the core implementation shortcut before it is taught.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can cargo-cult a groupby/transform expression without being able to predict which group a row belongs to or why the result aligns back to the original rows.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The expression is central to classifying conflicts, not decorative syntax.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use a small dict/set-based conflict detector with already learned constructs in S16, then teach groupby/transform from first principles in S17.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose defines an exact duplicate by the relevant columns and says conflict checks should cover each attribute that must agree. The code calls `df.duplicated(keep=False)` with no subset, so every column is relevant, and checks only `region` for conflict.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The executable classifier is narrower/different from the contract it claims to demonstrate. Provenance columns such as batch/source would prevent otherwise business-identical rows from being classified as exact duplicates.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can miss duplicate business records merely because provenance columns differ, or miss conflicts that occur in attributes other than region.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The next action—dedupe versus quarantine—depends on correct classification before deletion.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Declare `exact_cols` and `conflict_attrs` explicitly from the contract; use `duplicated(subset=exact_cols, keep=False)` and evaluate every conflict attribute with an explicit missing-value policy.

confirmed_findings.evidence: For two C001 rows with scores 0.9 and 0.4 from sources a/b, the lesson resolves the key with `drop_duplicates(key, keep='first')`. No source-priority, timestamp, authoritative-system or review rule explains why input order should win.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Input order is silently promoted into a business-resolution policy.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can choose whichever conflicting row happened to arrive first and treat that arbitrary ordering as a defensible master-record resolution.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: S17 is told to consume `clean`; arbitrary conflict resolution therefore contaminates downstream joins and analysis.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: For unresolved conflicts, quarantine the whole key and exclude it from clean. Demonstrate promotion only after a deterministic documented rule such as authoritative-source priority or reviewed timestamp.

confirmed_findings.evidence: `quarantine = df.loc[dup_mask]` contains both C001 rows, while `clean = df.drop_duplicates(key, keep='first')` also contains the first C001 row. For the three-row example, clean has 2 rows and quarantine has 2 rows: one source row is counted in both sets.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Set/disjointness intuition and row-count reconciliation from prior course goals.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The two outputs called clean and quarantine are not mutually exclusive even though quarantine is later defined as rejected rows.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can report `rows_clean + rows_quarantine > rows_in`, double-count excluded data, and feed a quarantined row into S17.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: This directly breaks the gate's promised loss accounting and the meaning of quarantine.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Make outputs disjoint by default: unresolved duplicate-key groups go entirely to quarantine; only a row explicitly resolved/promoted leaves quarantine and enters clean, with an audit event.

confirmed_findings.evidence: `stripped = df['region_raw'].str.strip()` can preserve missing values, but the following list comprehension calls `x.upper()` and `x.title()` unconditionally. `None`/`pd.NA` therefore raises instead of preserving or classifying the null.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: T1-A has just established that nullable fields are normal and must follow policy.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The normalizer is incompatible with the section's own null model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can apply the canonical normalizer to an optional missing region and crash the batch instead of preserving null or routing it according to policy.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Null handling is supposed to be the first gate that every later transformation respects.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use a null-safe `norm_region(x)` that returns `pd.NA` for missing inputs before applying `.upper()`/`.title()` to actual strings.

confirmed_findings.evidence: `norm_money('abc')` becomes NaN through `or 'nan'` with no reason/count; malformed values such as repeated separators can raise ValueError; `parse_fecha` converts any unrecognized date to `pd.NaT`. The lesson preserves raw columns but emits no normalization-failure mask, code or quarantine evidence.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Invalid normalization outcomes are either silently converted to missing or crash outside the promised gate evidence model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can transform bad source tokens into NaN/NaT without counting the failure and believe preserving `raw` alone satisfies «nunca arreglar en silencio».
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The gate cannot quantify loss or explain why a row failed if the normalization stage does not emit reasons.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: After parsing, compute `raw.notna() & parsed.isna()` failure masks (or return value+reason) and attach structured reason codes/counts; catch deliberate parse failures at the quality boundary.

confirmed_findings.evidence: S16 uses median imputation and then introduces quantiles, IQR, the 1.5×IQR rule and mentions z-score, while the authoritative roadmap schedules center, dispersion and quantiles for S18. No local explanation establishes what a median/quantile/IQR represents or why 1.5 is a candidate heuristic.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic arithmetic; inferential/descriptive-statistics vocabulary is not yet creditable.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner is asked to execute statistical formulas before the concepts that make them interpretable are taught.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can memorize `1.5 * IQR` as a universal truth detector or use median merely as a magic function without understanding the decision it encodes.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The section explicitly warns that statistical outliers are not business errors, so the statistical flag mechanism needs enough meaning to support that distinction.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Give one bounded micro-model: median = middle value after ordering; Q1/Q3 split the lower/upper quarters; IQR=Q3-Q1; 1.5×IQR is a conventional candidate flag, not a business verdict. Defer z-score and deeper statistics to S18.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose defines schema contract as column presence, expected dtypes and field nullability. `contracts.py` checks only a set of expected column names; it never verifies dtype or nullable policy.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S15 schema was already MISCONCEPTION_RISK and cannot be assumed executable.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: S16 repeats the schema vocabulary but still does not make the declared contract dimensions executable.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can pass the lesson's 'schema' gate with a required numeric column encoded as arbitrary strings or containing prohibited nulls.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: S16 is the section designated to repair/strengthen data contracts before S17 consumes the clean dataset.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Represent each required column with at least expected dtype + nullable flag and evaluate those properties before cross-field rules; report structured violations.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The code computes `drift = expected - set(df.columns)` but immediately evaluates `df['fin'] < df['inicio']` and `df['monto'] < 0` before printing/returning the drift. If `fin` is missing, the example raises raw `KeyError('fin')`, exactly the outcome the prose says should be avoided.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The supposed fail-closed guard is calculated but not used to gate downstream field access.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can copy the canonical pattern, detect the missing column correctly, and still crash before producing the promised operator-facing diagnostic.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Explainable schema drift is the section-level gate in the roadmap.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Check and report missing required columns first; if any exist, stop further field rules and return/emit a structured fail result before accessing those columns.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says each rule returns a failure mask plus a readable error code for quarantine. The code only prints index lists under labels `cross_fail_idx` and `neg_idx`; it never constructs a quarantine reason field or rule-code record.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The output shape required to connect a rule failure to T4-B quarantine is missing.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can identify row 1 as bad but still not know how to produce the promised row-level reason evidence when several rules fail.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Quarantine is only auditable if failures carry stable reasons.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Create a small violations table/list with row index/key, rule code and optional detail, then derive quarantine from those violations.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose promises null/duplicate/schema-failure rates in addition to row counts. The code manually constructs one-row clean and quarantine DataFrames and emits only rows_in, rows_clean, rows_quarantine and pass; none of the metrics are computed from the earlier checks.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic counts/rates; quality checks from this lesson.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The final report is a fabricated example rather than evidence generated by the gate.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can hard-code plausible metrics independently of the data-quality rules and still believe the quality suite is operational.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The roadmap explicitly requires quantified loss; this is the evidence surface an operator would rely on.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Derive all metrics from the same raw input and rule outputs, include per-rule counts/rates, and assert row conservation/disjointness where the policy partitions rows.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose promises `exit code != 0` together with JSON metrics when pass=False. The code only prints JSON and returns normally; the process therefore has no demonstrated non-zero status. The effective S10 ledger marks process exit status as MISCONCEPTION_RISK, so S16 cannot inherit this mechanism as mastered.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Process exit mapping is not creditable from S10.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A critical operational behavior is asserted but never implemented at the process boundary.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can equate printing `"pass": false` with making an orchestrator/OS observe failure, repeating an earlier course misconception.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Fail-closed batch operation depends on a machine-readable failure signal, not only a human-readable JSON field.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Show a minimal `main() -> int` that emits metrics first and then exits non-zero on failed gate, e.g. `raise SystemExit(main())`; keep structured output available before exit.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson defines audit trail as append-only—events are never modified or deleted—but the only implementation is a normal Python list, which permits assignment, deletion, insert and clear with no guard or persistence.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A behavioral governance property is attributed to an unconstrained mutable container.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can believe that storing events in a list makes the record append-only or tamper-resistant.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Auditability claims should distinguish an instructional convention from an enforced storage property.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State that the in-memory list models event order by convention only; expose only an append API in the lab and defer durable/tamper-evident enforcement, or implement a constrained append-only writer.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Operational English terms such as `cap`, `runbook`, `stakeholder`, `schema drift` and `cross-field` appear with uneven Spanish explanation. Some core terms are defined, but these remain necessary to interpret the gate policy.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: General Spanish and earlier Python/data vocabulary; these operations terms are not baseline knowledge.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner must decode domain jargon while also learning the quality mechanism.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can understand the code yet not know what a `cap`, `runbook` or cross-field rule is supposed to mean operationally.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: These are policy-bearing terms, not optional industry color.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Introduce Spanish-first once: `tope (cap)`, `manual operativo (runbook)`, `parte interesada/responsable (stakeholder)`, `desviación de esquema (schema drift)`, `regla entre campos (cross-field)`.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: El job venía fallando... `monto.fillna(0)`... ticket promedio aparece más bajo...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Un job que deja de fallar no necesariamente produce datos correctos. Si `monto` falta y alguien ejecuta `monto.fillna(0)`, el proceso puede continuar, pero ahora un valor ausente se transformó en un cero observado y puede bajar el ticket promedio. El problema queda oculto porque el programa termina sin error.
paragraph_audit.rationale: El caso inicial hace visible la diferencia entre ejecución exitosa y calidad semántica; solo se vuelve un poco más causal.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: `NaN` significa «no sé»; cero significa «sé que es cero».
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En estas columnas pandas puede usar `NaN` como **marca de valor faltante**. Esa marca no explica por qué falta: el valor pudo venir ausente del archivo, fallar durante una conversión o quedar indefinido en un cálculo. Cero, en cambio, es un valor observado. Por eso cada campo necesita dos decisiones separadas: si el faltante está permitido y, si lo está, qué significa y qué acción está autorizada.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Separa sentinel técnico de significado de negocio y prepara una política de null más rica que required/optional.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: nunca arreglar en silencio... métrica, indicador o fila apartada en cuarentena...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: De ahí sale la regla que gobierna la sección: **nunca arreglar en silencio**. Cada transformación debe producir evidencia junto con el dato: un conteo, un indicador por fila o una razón de cuarentena. Así puedes reconstruir qué cambió, cuántas filas afectó y por qué.
paragraph_audit.rationale: La regla es correcta; se hace más explícita la cadena dato→transformación→evidencia.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: duplicados... conflicto... valores extremos...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Los duplicados y los valores extremos exigen la misma disciplina. Primero clasifica qué ocurrió; después decide. Dos filas idénticas pueden colapsarse bajo una regla documentada, mientras que dos filas con la misma clave y atributos incompatibles forman un conflicto. Un valor extremo puede ser error o caso legítimo: se marca antes de decidir.
paragraph_audit.rationale: El modelo conceptual es defendible y coherente con el roadmap.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Cuando el contrato se rompe, el trabajo se detiene y publica sus métricas... fail-closed.
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Cuando una regla bloqueante se rompe, el **quality gate** debe producir primero evidencia estructurada —reglas fallidas, filas afectadas y métricas— y después devolver un resultado de fallo que impida promover esas filas como limpias. En T4 ensamblaremos esas decisiones en un único flujo `entrada → reglas → clean/quarantine → métricas → pass/fail`.
paragraph_audit.rationale: La definición debe anticipar el mecanismo integrado que la versión actual no demuestra.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Bloque de referencia. Orden de los subtemas y criterio de cierre.
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Bloque de referencia: orden de los subtemas y criterio de cierre.
paragraph_audit.rationale: No hay defecto material.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: T1 trata la ausencia... T4 cierra con contratos y quality gate.
paragraph_audit.improved_version: T1 decide qué faltantes están permitidos y qué acciones admite cada campo; T2 clasifica duplicados y conflictos; T3 normaliza sin perder el raw y separa extremos estadísticos de errores de dominio; T4 integra las reglas en un gate con evidencia.
paragraph_audit.rationale: La secuencia coincide con el roadmap; se explicita integración.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: conjunto limpio... debe poder re-ejecutarse y dar los mismos números.
paragraph_audit.improved_version: El cierre no es solo obtener un DataFrame limpio: con la misma entrada, versión de contrato y reglas, el gate debe reconstruir el mismo `clean`, la misma `quarantine` y las mismas métricas. Además, `clean` y `quarantine` no deben contar la misma fila simultáneamente.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Hace verificable reproducibilidad y row accounting.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Cada campo... required u optional...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Cada campo necesita al menos dos piezas de política. **Required/optional** indica si el faltante está permitido. La **acción de null** indica qué hacer cuando aparece: bloquear/cuarentenar, conservar el null o imputar bajo una regla específica. `optional` no significa automáticamente `imputable`.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Evita que optionalidad se convierta en autorización de inventar datos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: dict `{campo: 'required'|'optional'}`...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Representa el contrato con una entrada por campo que guarde su requisito y su acción, por ejemplo `{'monto': {'required': True, 'on_null': 'quarantine'}}`. Mide `isna()` antes de transformar. Un campo required con null produce una violación; un optional sigue la acción documentada en vez de recibir un default por costumbre.
paragraph_audit.rationale: El contrato ejecutable captura la decisión que la versión binaria pierde.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: cliente_id y monto required; email optional...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En el fixture, `cliente_id` y `monto` son required. `email` es optional y su ausencia se **conserva y reporta**; no se imputa porque el contrato no ha autorizado una sustitución. Así se ve que permitir un null y reemplazarlo son decisiones distintas.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Añade un ejemplo negativo de la confusión central.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: indicador de ausencia... preserva señal...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Si el contrato autoriza imputar un campo, crea antes un indicador como `descuento_was_null`. Ese indicador conserva qué filas fueron modificadas y evita confundir el valor imputado con uno observado.
paragraph_audit.rationale: La idea es correcta y causal.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: cap 30–40%... null_rate > cap...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: El **tope de imputación (cap)** limita el porcentaje máximo de filas que una regla ya autorizada puede rellenar. No decide si el campo es imputable. Primero el contrato debe autorizar método y significado; después el tope bloquea la operación si el volumen de faltantes es demasiado alto.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Define cap y separa autorización semántica de límite cuantitativo.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: 2/5 null... cap=0.4... fillna(mediana)...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Si `descuento` está declarado explícitamente como `optional_impute` y su tasa es 2/5, un cap de 0.4 permite ejecutar la regla elegida. Si la regla usa la **mediana**, recuerda que es el valor central de los datos observados al ordenarlos; se calcula antes de rellenar. Para `monto` required, el cap no cambia la política: la fila se bloquea o cuarentena.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Explica median de forma mínima y evita optional=>impute.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Duplicado exacto... Conflicto...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Un **duplicado exacto de negocio** coincide en las columnas que el contrato declara relevantes. Un **conflicto** comparte la clave de negocio pero difiere en uno o más atributos que deberían coincidir. Primero clasifica; después decide si deduplicar, resolver o cuarentenar.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Concepto válido; la precisión 'de negocio' prepara subset explícito.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: duplicated(keep=False)... groupby(...).transform('nunique')...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Declara primero `exact_cols` y `conflict_attrs`. Para exactos usa `duplicated(subset=exact_cols, keep=False)`. Para conflictos, en esta sección recorre las filas con diccionarios/conjuntos ya conocidos y registra, por cada clave, qué valores distintos aparecen en cada atributo. `groupby` y `transform` llegan en S17; no son requisito para aprender la política de calidad aquí.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Repara el contrato del detector y elimina el leak de S17.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: C001 repetido exacto... C002 Cusco vs Madrid...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En el fixture, `exact_cols = ['cliente_id','region','score']`: las dos filas de C001 son exactas aunque una futura columna de provenance difiera. C002 comparte clave pero tiene dos regiones y queda marcado como conflicto. Si otro atributo contractual también difiere, debe aparecer en la evidencia.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Hace observable qué columnas determinan cada clase.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: duplicados de clave van a cuarentena... no se eliminan...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Cuando una clave que debería ser 1:1 aparece varias veces, conserva **todas** sus versiones en cuarentena y excluye inicialmente esa clave de `clean`. Solo una regla de resolución documentada puede promover una versión —por ejemplo, una fuente autoritativa o una decisión humana— y esa promoción deja un evento.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Evita resolución por posición y solapamiento.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: clean = drop_duplicates(key, keep=...)... quarantine = filas con clave duplicada...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: No uses `drop_duplicates(key, keep='first')` como política de conflicto. Construye `quarantine` con el grupo conflictivo y `clean` con las claves no conflictivas; si después una regla resuelve el caso, mueve/promueve explícitamente una versión y registra el motivo. La lista de eventos del laboratorio modela el orden por convención; una lista de Python no impone append-only por sí sola.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Corrige dos garantías falsas sin exigir infraestructura durable.

paragraph_audit.improved_version: Con C001=0.9 desde `src=a` y C001=0.4 desde `src=b`, no hay base para elegir 0.9 solo porque llegó primero. Hasta que el contrato declare qué fuente o revisión manda, ambas filas permanecen en cuarentena y C001 no aparece en `clean`.
paragraph_audit.rationale: El ejemplo debe enseñar incertidumbre/resolución, no input-order policy.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Normalización... strings, locale, fechas... raw...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Normalizar significa convertir representaciones equivalentes a una forma canónica sin inventar información. Cada normalizador recibe el `raw`, conserva los nulls según la política y devuelve también evidencia cuando un valor no puede interpretarse. `raw` conserva el origen; un código de fallo explica qué pasó.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Integra T1 con T3 y evita que raw sea sustituto de error reporting.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Contrato de montos PEN sintéticos... reglas separadores...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Para el fixture PEN, documenta exactamente las reglas de separadores y aplícalas solo a los formatos permitidos. Si un token no cumple (`abc`, separadores repetidos, etc.), no lo conviertas silenciosamente a NaN ni dejes escapar un `ValueError`: marca `invalid_money_format` y conserva `monto_raw`.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Convierte parser ad hoc en regla de calidad observable.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: fechas multi-formato... parsea probando formatos...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Para fechas, prueba únicamente los formatos documentados. Un null permitido sigue siendo null; una cadena presente que no coincide con ninguno produce `invalid_date_format` y queda contada o en cuarentena. Aplica la misma regla a región: prueba missing antes de llamar `.upper()`/`.title()`.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Distingue ausencia válida de error de parse y hace el código null-safe.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: IQR y z-score solo identifican candidatos...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Un extremo puede ser estadístico sin ser un error de negocio. Aquí usamos una sola heurística para marcar candidatos: Q1 y Q3 son los cuartiles que delimitan aproximadamente el 25% y 75% de los datos ordenados; `IQR = Q3 - Q1`. Valores fuera de `Q1 - 1.5·IQR` y `Q3 + 1.5·IQR` se revisan, no se borran. El factor 1.5 es una convención, no una ley del dominio.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Da el mínimo modelo mental necesario y elimina z-score prematuro.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: mantén máscaras stat_outlier y domain_error...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Mantén separados `stat_outlier` y `domain_error`. `stat_outlier` solo dice «esta observación quedó lejos según la heurística IQR»; `domain_error` aplica una regla del fixture, por ejemplo `monto ∈ [0, 10000]`. Solo la política de dominio decide bloquear; la estadística puede pedir revisión.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Aclara actor/criterio/consecuencia.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: 5000 cola plausible y -1 error...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En `[10, 12, 11, 13, 5000, -1]`, la regla IQR marca 5000 y -1 como candidatos porque están lejos del centro del pequeño fixture. La regla de dominio `[0,10000]` rechaza únicamente -1; 5000 queda como extremo plausible para revisión. S18 profundizará por qué funcionan cuartiles y dispersión.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Hace explícito que el resultado estadístico es provisional y pequeño.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: schema: columnas presentes, dtypes, nullability... cross-field...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Convierte el schema en reglas ejecutables: para cada columna guarda `required`, `dtype` y `nullable`; después agrega reglas **entre campos (cross-field)** con un `rule_code` estable. Cada evaluación debe producir qué fila/campo falló y por qué, no solo una máscara anónima.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Alinea definición con evidencia ejecutable.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Ante schema drift... gate falla con nombre... no KeyError...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Ante **desviación de esquema (schema drift)**, valida primero las columnas obligatorias. Si falta alguna, emite los nombres faltantes y termina esa evaluación antes de ejecutar reglas que accedan a esas columnas. Las columnas extra siguen una política explícita: permitir, advertir o fallar.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Repara el orden causal que hoy produce KeyError.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: expected... cross_fail_idx... neg_idx...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En el ejemplo, primero valida `{inicio, fin, monto}` y sus tipos/nullability. Solo si esa fase pasa, evalúa `fin >= inicio` y `monto >= 0`. Produce violaciones como `{'row': 1, 'rule_code': 'fin_before_inicio'}` y `{'row': 1, 'rule_code': 'monto_negative'}` para que T4-B pueda construir la cuarentena.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Une schema, control flow y reason codes.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: rows_in, rows_clean, rows_quarantine, tasas... pass...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Las métricas deben salir del mismo run que produjo las decisiones: `rows_in`, `rows_clean`, `rows_quarantine`, conteos/tasas por regla y `pass`. Comprueba además que una fila no esté simultáneamente en `clean` y `quarantine`, y explica cualquier diferencia entre `rows_in` y la suma de destinos.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Evita métricas inventadas y double-counting.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: audit trail append-only... exit code !=0 + JSON...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: La cuarentena conserva la fila y un `reason_code`. El audit del laboratorio es una secuencia de eventos que el programa **trata por convención** como append-only; una lista no lo hace inmutable. Al terminar, el programa escribe primero el JSON de métricas y luego devuelve un código de proceso: 0 si pasa y distinto de 0 si una regla bloqueante falla.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Separa convención de enforcement y enseña el process boundary.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: 2 filas entrada, 1 limpia, 1 cuarentena... S17 solo consume clean...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Ejecuta el gate sobre dos filas reales: una pasa y otra falla `null_required_monto`. De ese único flujo deben salir `clean=1`, `quarantine=1`, la razón, `pass=false` y el código de proceso de fallo. S17 consume únicamente `clean`; el reporte conserva cuántas filas quedaron fuera y por qué.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Cierra la sección demostrando la composición prometida.

code_audit.observed: Counts required nulls correctly for the fixture, but policy only stores required/optional and directly indexes every policy column without schema-presence guard.
code_audit.improved_direction: Use field policy with required + on_null action; schema-presence check before per-column isna.

code_audit.observed: Boundary rate==cap follows stated `>` policy and output is correct, but the code makes cap plus optionality the effective authorization to median-impute.
code_audit.improved_direction: Separate semantic authorization (`optional_impute`) from numerical cap; microdefine median or use a domain constant.

code_audit.observed: Fixture output is correct, but `duplicated()` uses all columns and conflict detection uses only region plus not-yet-taught groupby/transform.
code_audit.improved_direction: Declare exact_cols/conflict_attrs and use prior-known dict/set logic until S17 teaches groupby.

code_audit.observed: For 3 input rows, clean has 2 and quarantine has 2; the first C001 row belongs to both. `keep='first'` resolves conflicting scores only by input order.
code_audit.improved_direction: Quarantine unresolved duplicate-key groups entirely; promote one version only under documented deterministic resolution and remove it from quarantine.

code_audit.observed: Missing region raises on `.upper()`/`.title()`. `norm_money('abc')` becomes NaN without reason; some malformed separators raise ValueError; unrecognized dates become NaT without failure evidence.
code_audit.improved_direction: Null-safe normalizers plus parsed-value/failure-reason outputs or raw-present→parsed-null failure masks.

code_audit.observed: Displayed output is technically correct for [10,12,11,13,5000,-1], but median/quantile/IQR statistical machinery is used before S18 teaches it.
code_audit.improved_direction: Add bounded quartile/IQR mental model, label 1.5×IQR a candidate heuristic, defer z-score/deeper stats.

code_audit.observed: Checks only required column names; no dtype/nullability. Missing `fin` produces drift set but then raw KeyError before diagnostic. Outputs index lists, not structured rule codes/quarantine evidence.
code_audit.improved_direction: Validate schema dimensions first, return structured fail if drift, then evaluate cross-field rules into row+rule_code violations.

code_audit.observed: Clean/quarantine are hand-authored rather than produced by rules; promised null/dup/schema rates are absent; pass=false is printed but no nonzero process exit occurs; ordinary list does not enforce append-only.
code_audit.improved_direction: Run one integrated gate, derive metrics and audit events, emit JSON, then map pass/fail to actual process exit; label list append-only as convention unless enforced.

rules: Do not inherit groupby/transform/nunique from S16; they were used before teaching and remain MENTION_ONLY.
Do not trust S16 clean/quarantine outputs as disjoint or reconciled; S17 joins must start from an explicitly validated partition.
Do not promote conflicting duplicate-key rows by keep='first' before join cardinality work.
S15 Index/concat/join misconceptions remain active when S17 teaches joins; repair from first principles.
Schema dtype/nullability enforcement remains MISCONCEPTION_RISK and cannot be assumed.
Normalization failures (invalid money/date/nullable region) remain unsafe; S17 must not treat normalized columns as validated merely because they exist.
Median/quantile/IQR/z-score remain MENTION_ONLY; S18 owns their full mental model.
Do not assume one-row-per-client cardinality applies to transaction tables.
S17 reconciliation must explicitly prove row counts/denominators before and after joins.
